annotations.description:
Allows clients to store small amounts of arbitrary data.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

disabled.description: If disabled is set to true, functionality is disabled for this connection. Repository based API methods and webhooks processing for repositories in this connection will be disabled.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: Immutable. The resource name of the connection.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

bitbucket_cloud_config.description: Configuration for connections to Bitbucket Cloud.

bitbucket_cloud_config.webhook_secret_se.description: Required. Immutable. SecretManager resource containing the webhook secret used to verify webhook events, formatted as 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.
bitbucket_cloud_config.webhook_secret_se.rationale: Webhook secrets must be restricted to approved versions stored securely in Secret Manager to prevent unauthorized access and ensure trusted communication between Bitbucket and Cloud Build.

bitbucket_cloud_config.workspace.description: The Bitbucket Cloud Workspace ID to be connected to Google Cloud Platform.

bitbucket_cloud_config.authorizer_creden.description: Required. An access token with the 'webhook', 'repository', 'repository:admin' and 'pullrequest' scope access. It can be either a workspace, project or repository access token. It's recommended to use a system account to generate these credentials.
Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

bitbucket_cloud_config.read_authorizer_c.description: Required. An access token with the 'repository' access. It can be either a workspace, project or repository access token. It's recommended to use a system account to generate the credentials.
Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

bitbucket_data_center_config.description: Configuration for connections to Bitbucket Data Center.

bitbucket_data_center_config.host_uri.description: The URI of the Bitbucket Data Center host this connection is for.

bitbucket_data_center_config.ssl_ca.description: SSL certificate to use for requests to the Bitbucket Data Center.
bitbucket_data_center_config.ssl_ca.rationale: The ssl_ca ensures that connections to Bitbucket Data Center are verified using a trusted certificate authority, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks and ensuring secure communication.

bitbucket_data_center_config.webhook_sec.description: Required. Immutable. SecretManager resource containing the webhook secret used to verify webhook events, formatted as 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.
bitbucket_data_center_config.webhook_sec.rationale: The webhook secret must be stored in a secure secret version to ensure that incoming webhook requests are authenticated and protected from tampering or unauthorized triggering of build pipelines.

bitbucket_data_center_config.authorizer_.description: Required. A http access token with the 'REPO_ADMIN' scope access.
Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

bitbucket_data_center_config.read_author.description: Required. A http access token with the 'REPO_READ' access.
Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

bitbucket_data_center_config.service_dir.description: Configuration for using Service Directory to privately connect to a Bitbucket Data Center. This should only be set if the Bitbucket Data Center is hosted on-premises and not reachable by public internet. If this field is left empty, calls to the Bitbucket Data Center will be made over the public internet.
Required. The Service Directory service name. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/namespaces/{namespace}/services/{service}.

github_config.app_installation_id.rationale: The GitHub App installation ID identifying the integration. This is an identifier referencing an external integration; we do not constrain its value (it is team/org-specific), so it is not a policy target.

github_config.authorizer_credential.description: OAuth credential of the account that authorized the Cloud Build GitHub App. It is recommended to use a robot account instead of a human user account. The OAuth token must be tied to the Cloud Build GitHub App.

github_config.authorizer_credential.oaut.description: A SecretManager resource containing the OAuth token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

github_enterprise_config.description: Configuration for connections to an instance of GitHub Enterprise.

github_enterprise_config.app_id.description: Id of the GitHub App created from the manifest.

github_enterprise_config.app_installatio.description: ID of the installation of the GitHub App.
github_enterprise_config.app_installatio.rationale: The GitHub Enterprise App installation ID identifying the integration. This is an identifier referencing an external integration; we do not constrain its value, so it is not a policy target.

github_enterprise_config.app_slug.description: The URL-friendly name of the GitHub App.
github_enterprise_config.app_slug.rationale: The slug identifying the GitHub Enterprise App. This is an identifier referencing an external app; we do not constrain its value, so it is not a policy target.

github_enterprise_config.host_uri.description: Required. The URI of the GitHub Enterprise host this connection is for.
github_enterprise_config.host_uri.rationale: The URI of the GitHub Enterprise host the connection targets. This is a reference to an external endpoint; a generic platform policy cannot pin a team/org-specific host, so it is not a policy target.

github_enterprise_config.private_key_sec.description: SecretManager resource containing the private key of the GitHub App, formatted as 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.
github_enterprise_config.private_key_sec.rationale: The private key must be stored in a secure and approved secret version to protect authentication credentials and prevent unauthorized access.

github_enterprise_config.ssl_ca.description: SSL certificate to use for requests to GitHub Enterprise.
github_enterprise_config.ssl_ca.rationale: Provides the SSL/CA certificate used to verify TLS connections to GitHub Enterprise. Requiring it to be set ensures the connection's server certificate is validated, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks — a secure-transport control (matching the Bitbucket ssl_ca, which is marked true).

github_enterprise_config.webhook_secret_.description: SecretManager resource containing the webhook secret of the GitHub App, formatted as 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.
github_enterprise_config.webhook_secret_.rationale: The webhook secret must be securely stored and validated to ensure webhook events are authenticated and protected from tampering or unauthorized triggers.

github_enterprise_config.service_directo.description: Configuration for using Service Directory to privately connect to a GitHub Enterprise server. This should only be set if the GitHub Enterprise server is hosted on-premises and not reachable by public internet. If this field is left empty, calls to the GitHub Enterprise server will be made over the public internet.
Required. The Service Directory service name. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/namespaces/{namespace}/services/{service}.

gitlab_config.description: Configuration for connections to gitlab.com or an instance of GitLab Enterprise.

gitlab_config.host_uri.description: The URI of the GitLab Enterprise host this connection is for. If not specified, the default value is https://gitlab.com.

gitlab_config.ssl_ca.description: SSL certificate to use for requests to GitLab Enterprise.

gitlab_config.webhook_secret_secret_vers.description: Required. Immutable. SecretManager resource containing the webhook secret of a GitLab Enterprise project, formatted as 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

gitlab_config.authorizer_credential.description: Required. A GitLab personal access token with the 'api' scope access.

gitlab_config.authorizer_credential.user.description: Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

gitlab_config.read_authorizer_credential.description: Required. A GitLab personal access token with the minimum 'read_api' scope access.
Required. A SecretManager resource containing the user token that authorizes the Cloud Build connection. Format: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

gitlab_config.service_directory_config.description: Configuration for using Service Directory to privately connect to a GitLab Enterprise server. This should only be set if the GitLab Enterprise server is hosted on-premises and not reachable by public internet. If this field is left empty, calls to the GitLab Enterprise server will be made over the public internet.

gitlab_config.service_directory_config.s.description: Required. The Service Directory service name. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/namespaces/{namespace}/services/{service}.
